source_name: ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Acute Care Settings

entries.rationale: IV vasoactive catecholamine; dosing/infusion-rate errors rapidly cause severe hypertension, arrhythmias, or tissue ischemia.
IV/IO adrenergic agonist requires double-check for concentration (1:10,000 vs 1:1,000) and pump rate; IM anaphylaxis auto-injector/IM is excluded from IV class.
IV adrenergic agonist (look-alike Tall Man pair DOPamine/DOBUTamine); infusion errors cause tachyarrhythmias or hemodynamic collapse.

entries.ismpCategory: Inotropic medications, IV / Adrenergic agonists, IV
entries.rationale: IV inotropic catecholamine (look-alike Tall Man pair DOBUTamine/DOPamine).
Explicitly listed on ISMP 2024 Specific Medications (IV and IO) due to severe vasoconstriction and dose-unit confusion (units/min vs units/hr).
IV beta-blocker listed under Adrenergic antagonists, IV; oral metoprolol is not high-alert.
IV antiarrhythmic; rapid non-arrest bolus or miscalculation risks severe hypotension, bradycardia, and arrhythmias.
IV antiarrhythmic producing transient asystole; requires rapid push protocol and cardiac monitoring.
IV digoxin is listed under Inotropic medications, IV; oral digoxin is tracked separately as an NTI/TDM drug.
Oral vitamin K antagonist with narrow therapeutic index and fatal hemorrhage risk.

entries.ismpCategory: Antithrombotic agents — Low molecular weight heparins
entries.rationale: LMWH anticoagulant with bleeding and spinal/epidural hematoma risk.
High-risk anticoagulant prone to weight-based/vial-strength dosing errors and hemorrhage.

entries.ismpCategory: Antithrombotic agents — DOACs and factor Xa inhibitors
entries.rationale: Direct factor Xa inhibitor carrying major/fatal bleeding risk if unadjusted for renal/age/weight criteria.

entries.ismpCategory: Antithrombotic agents — DOACs and factor Xa inhibitors
entries.rationale: Direct factor Xa inhibitor with strict renal/hepatic contraindications and hemorrhage risk.
Severe hypoglycemia and hypokalemia risk across SC and IV routes.
Long-acting insulin with fatal hypoglycemia risk on wrong-dose or look-alike insulin mix-ups.
Oral sulfonylurea included under ISMP 2024 Hypoglycemics, oral due to prolonged severe hypoglycemia risk, especially in renal impairment.
Opioid analgesic across IV/SC/PO routes; respiratory depression and 10x concentration errors.
Potent opioid dosed in mcg; respiratory depression and fatal mg-vs-mcg error risk.
Opioid agonist carrying respiratory depression, seizure, and serotonin toxicity risks across routes.

entries.ismpCategory: Moderate sedation agents, IV / Pediatric oral sedation
entries.rationale: IV moderate sedation agent (and oral moderate/minimal sedation for children) carrying apnea/respiratory arrest risk.
Explicitly cited in ISMP 2024 moderate sedation agents, IV; risk of profound bradycardia and hypotension.

entries.ismpCategory: Anesthetic agents, general, inhaled and IV
entries.rationale: IV general anesthetic carrying rapid apnea, hypotension, and PRIS toxicity.
Explicitly listed on ISMP 2024 Specific Medications (injection); overdose causes respiratory paralysis and cardiac arrest.
Explicitly listed on ISMP 2024 Specific Medications (IV only); uterine tachysystole and fetal distress risk.
Explicitly listed on ISMP 2024 Specific Medications (injection concentrate); undiluted push or excessive rate causes fatal cardiac arrest. Oral KCl is excluded.
Parenteral cytotoxic antineoplastic agent.

entries.ismpCategory: Chemotherapeutic agents / Methotrexate, oral, non-oncologic use
entries.rationale: Listed under both Chemotherapy and Specific Medications (oral non-oncologic weekly regimen mix-up risk).
